independent_source.publisher: U.S. Federal Trade Commission, Office of Commissioner Rohit Chopra
independent_source.quote: The company enhanced their facial recognition technology by allegedly baiting consumers into using Ever, a “free” app

verdicts.note: Statement dated 2021-01-08. This is the primary document itself and the same URL the profile cites; no second source quoting it was reachable without search.

The fact is right (page dated 2026-09-23) but the quote is a product tagline that shows neither the date nor that Paravision announced it. Words that would: 'September 23, 2026 — Paravision, a leader in trusted Identity AI, today announced the Paravision ISO/ICAO Image Quality Suite'. The profile's status rests on a vendor page alone; see everalbum-v001 for an independent September 2026 source.

Quote matches the page dated 2026-01-26. As 'newest dated corporate event' it holds on what was reachable: later newsroom items (March, August, September 2026) are product and benchmark news, not corporate events. Without search a later layoff or funding event cannot be excluded.
The quote stops before what the 25% did. The complaint's next words are 'when presented with the pop-up message chose to turn face recognition off'.

The quote shows only '13 billion photos and videos'; 'tens of millions of users in 95 countries' is in the next words of the NBC sentence. NBC attributes the figure to Ever AI's news releases, which are not dated in the article, so 'said in 2019' is the article's date, not necessarily the release's. The source is tagged independent_press but here it relays the vendor (press_relayed); the claim's origin vendor_stated is right.

The two quotes together support it. The FTC letter's sentence begins 'Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act does not allow'; the quoted fragment omits 'Section 5' but the claim is right. Chopra frames the cause more narrowly (no Section 18 rule restating the precedent).

The quote ends at 'confirming it deleted the data', which does not show that the statements covered photos, embeddings and models. Words that would: 'confirming it deleted the data required under Order § III (A), (B), and (C)' (III A photos/videos, B face embeddings, C Affected Work Product).

The report says 'Covered Information', an order-defined term for information from or about an individual consumer; the statement's 'any information' is a fair rendering. The claim is correctly framed as Paravision's own sworn statement.
Complaint quote supports it. The profile's second source (NBC News) quotes Ever's CEO, so it is the vendor relayed (press_relaying_vendor), not independent_press for this point.
The quote is cut after 'access control' and omits payments, which the statement names. The complaint continues ', and facilitating payments'.

The quote shows only that face images from users' photos were combined 'with facial images'; it does not show the dates, the public datasets or the four datasets. The same complaint sentence has 'Between September 2017 and August 2019' and 'obtained from publicly available datasets in order to create four new datasets'. Separately, its use for matrix.supply_models stretches the field: these were training inputs, not listed inventory, and storage-app uploads are not 'contributor_uploads' in the vocab's sense; the profile's own note admits this.

The quote shows B2B/B2G only; the 'offers nothing to individual consumers' half needs the next words, 'and does not offer any products or services to individual consumers'. The statement is in the present tense but rests on a 2022-05-05 filing.
The AI Principles quote matches the statement. The page date (2022-04-06) is the principles page's own date; the compliance report says they were first published in August 2020.
The words are the help article's as quoted in complaint para 9; the article was posted from July 2018. The statement could say it is known only through the FTC complaint.

Supports the statement. As support for contributor_pay_model 'none' it is indirect: 'free' describes the app's price to users, not the absence of payment to them, though no payment appears anywhere in the FTC record.
